title: Animation
objective: Build an animation loop with requestAnimationFrame, separate update and draw, and calculate speed and bouncing
story: The pictures on Pixel Planet have started to move! Like cartoons, games draw dozens of pictures one after another every second. Today you'll build an **animation loop** and make your ship move.

sections.title: How does animation work?
sections.body:
Every movement on the screen is really a set of pictures changing fast. In every **frame** three things happen:

1. Move the objects a little.
2. Erase the old picture.
3. Draw the new picture.

The browser gives us `requestAnimationFrame` (rAF for short) for this. It means: "run this function just before drawing the next picture". If the function asks for itself again every time, you get a loop that doesn't freeze the browser (usually 60 frames per second):

```js
function loop() {
  update();                    // calculate
  draw();                      // draw
  requestAnimationFrame(loop); // ask for the next frame
}
requestAnimationFrame(loop);
```

You can't animate with `while (true)`: the browser never gets a chance to draw and the page freezes.

sections.title: Separate update and draw
Speed and bouncing off the edges
Time difference (delta) and stopping

examples.title: Sliding square
examples.note: Set vx to 5: the square slides faster. What happens if you make it negative?

examples.title: Bouncing ball
examples.note: If you delete the clearRect line in draw, the ball leaves a trail behind it.

tasks.title: First movement
tasks.prompt:
The loop is ready; you write two functions:

- `update()`: adds `box.vx` to `box.x`.
- `draw()`: clears the canvas with `clearRect` and draws the box at `(box.x, box.y)` as a blue (`#4fc3f7`) square of size `size` × `size`.
hints: draw: ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height); then fillStyle and fillRect(box.x, box.y, box.size, box.size)

tasks.title: Bounce off the walls
tasks.prompt:
The ball should bounce off all four walls. The position already changes inside `update()`; add these below it:

- If the ball went past the right or left edge (`ball.x + ball.r > canvas.width` or `ball.x - ball.r < 0`), flip the sign of `vx`.
- Do the same for the top and bottom edges with `vy` and `canvas.height`.
hints: if (ball.x + ball.r > canvas.width || ball.x - ball.r < 0) { ball.vx = -ball.vx; }
Write the same with y, vy and canvas.height.

tasks.title: 120 pixels per second
tasks.prompt:
The rocket's speed is now in pixels **per second**: `speed: 120`.

- Write the `update(dt)` function: `dt` is the time that passed, in seconds; the rocket moves forward by `speed * dt`.
- Inside `loop(time)`, calculate `dt`: `(time - last) / 1000`. Then set `last = time` and call `update(dt)`.
hints: const dt = (time - last) / 1000; last = time; update(dt);

challenge.title: Stop / Start
challenge.prompt:
Stop and restart the animation with a button. The number returned by `requestAnimationFrame` is kept in `frameId`.

- If the button is clicked while `running` is true: stop it with `cancelAnimationFrame(frameId)`, set `running = false`, and the button's text becomes `Start`.
- If it's clicked while `running` is false: set `running = true`, restart the loop with `requestAnimationFrame(loop)`, and the button's text becomes `Stop`.

project_task.title: Ship movement
project_task.prompt:
The ship should now move back and forth by itself.

- `update()`: add `ship.vx` to `ship.x`. If the ship goes past the left edge (`ship.x < 0`), put it at `0`; if it goes past the right edge (`ship.x + ship.w > canvas.width`), put it at `canvas.width - ship.w`. In both cases, flip the sign of `vx`.
- `draw()` is ready: it draws the background, the ship and the stars.
- `loop()`: calls `update()` and `draw()` and asks for itself again with `requestAnimationFrame`. Don't forget to start the loop.
hints: if (ship.x + ship.w > canvas.width) { ship.x = canvas.width - ship.w; ship.vx = -ship.vx; }
